name: Hollis Fry
life: Hollis learned to ride again after a hip operation by delivering groceries for two neighbors. He remembers every doorway where he could set a bag down and lean for a moment. A delivery penalty can still feel like a verdict on his body. People around Lighthouse Cove know Hollis by a small Saturday habit. Hollis takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: The taped saddle tips to the left because my hip does. I made it through one delivery on the wrong bike before I began to limp. I want my lost delivery fee as much as my saddle.
appearance: Hollis has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow. Look for black hair twisted into a small knot. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a charcoal zip cardigan with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. In conversation Hollis rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Hollis is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Hollis is concerned.
agenda: To get the correct saddle back and the lost fee credited.
family: Kate Parra is Hollis’s half-sibling. Hollis picks the meeting place. Kate sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The housecoat commission*, Kate says, “I borrowed the pattern for my dad. He wants pockets large enough for Sunday's newspaper.”
connections: Marisol Vega. They meet a second time at the property counter to compare what the wrong saddle cost. Also in the story is Toby Lin (dispatcher).
